item.title: Pensacola Man Sentenced to 20 Years for Unregistered Firearms
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola man has been sentenced to two decades in federal prison for possessing unregistered firearms, according to a Department of Justice announcement. Alaisjah Perkins, 23, received the 20-year sentence on the gun charge. Federal prosecutors did not immediately provide additional details about the circumstances of the case or how law…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola man has been sentenced to two decades in federal prison for possessing unregistered firearms, according to a Department of Justice announcement.

Alaisjah Perkins, 23, received the 20-year sentence on the gun charge. Federal prosecutors did not immediately provide additional details about the circumstances of the case or how law enforcement discovered the unregistered weapons.

The sentencing adds to ongoing federal efforts to crack down on illegal firearms possession in the Pensacola area. Unregistered gun charges typically fall under federal jurisdiction and can carry substantial prison terms depending on the number of weapons involved and criminal history.

item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is closing out its 2026 summer Movie in the Parks series Friday night with a screening of Disney's Moana, according to WKRG News 5.

The final installment of the popular community event offers families one last chance to enjoy outdoor cinema as the season winds down. Movie in the Parks has been a staple summer activity across Santa Rosa County throughout 2026, drawing residents together for free entertainment.

Disney's Moana—the animated adventure about a Polynesian girl on a mission to save her people—wraps up a summer's worth of family-friendly films. Those planning to attend Friday should arrive early to secure a good spot, as these county events typically draw crowds.

item.content:encoded: The Pensacola Blue Wahoos couldn't recover from an early deficit in Wednesday night's game against the Biloxi Shuckers, dropping a 9-2 decision. The loss marked the first time since July 19th that Biloxi has been able to defeat Pensacola. The Shuckers struck quickly, scoring in the top of the first inning for the second consecutive night against the Wahoos, setting the tone early for what would become a dominant performance. The Blue Wahoos' offense struggled to generate the runs needed to mount a comeback, leaving them unable to close the gap as the game progressed.

item.title: Tate Volleyball Falls to Spanish Fort in Straight Sets
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The Toros dominated the contest, winning 25-14, 25-20, 25-14 in what marked a quick turnaround for the Aggies after a strong performance the night before. Tate had been riding high…
item.content:encoded:
The Tate High School Aggies couldn't keep their momentum rolling Wednesday evening, dropping a straight-sets match to visiting Spanish Fort High School in Cantonment. The Toros dominated the contest, winning 25-14, 25-20, 25-14 in what marked a quick turnaround for the Aggies after a strong performance the night before.

Tate had been riding high after picking up a 3-1 victory over Booker T. Washington on Tuesday, but the team ran into a tough test against the Alabama-based Spanish Fort squad. The Toros came into Escambia County and controlled play throughout the evening, showing little struggle in any of the three sets.

The loss drops Tate's record and sets up another opportunity to bounce back in upcoming matches as the volleyball season continues.

item.content:encoded:
The Century Neighborhood Watch is getting back to work this Thursday after taking a summer hiatus. The community group will convene at 5 p.m. at the Century Business Center, located at 150 Pond Street, Suite 5B, marking the restart of regular meetings for the North Escambia area.

The first gathering back will feature a special presentation from the Escambia County Sheriff's Office Narcotics Division, giving residents a chance to hear directly from law enforcement about drug-related concerns and community safety strategies in the region.

Neighborhood Watch members are encouraged to attend and reconnect with fellow residents focused on improving public safety and quality of life in Century.

item.title: Rainy stretch ahead for Pensacola area through weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A wet weather pattern is moving into the Pensacola area, with rain expected to increase Thursday and persist through Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. Thursday afternoon will see showers and thunderstorms likely between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., with conditions worsening Friday and Saturday. The heaviest rainfall is expected Friday and…
item.content:encoded:
A wet weather pattern is moving into the Pensacola area, with rain expected to increase Thursday and persist through Sunday, according to the National Weather Service.

Thursday afternoon will see showers and thunderstorms likely between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m., with conditions worsening Friday and Saturday. The heaviest rainfall is expected Friday and Saturday, when locally heavy downpours are possible. A few of the stronger storms could produce strong wind gusts, so residents should monitor conditions closely.

High rain chances are forecast to continue into Sunday as the wet pattern settles over the region. Those with outdoor plans should prepare for frequent showers and thunderstorms over the next several days and consider bringing activities indoors when possible.

item.content:encoded:
Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed a lawsuit against Netflix as part of a broader crackdown on major technology companies, according to reporting on the case.

The suit represents an expansion of Uthmeier's enforcement actions targeting big tech firms and their data handling practices. Details on the specific allegations against the streaming giant were not immediately disclosed.

This move aligns with similar legal actions the attorney general's office has pursued against other major technology companies. The case adds to a growing number of state-level challenges to tech industry practices nationwide.

No timeline for the suit's progression through Florida courts has been announced.

item.title: After 27 Years, Lt. Darren Snipes Retires from Escambia County Fire Rescue
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Lt. Darren Snipes wrapped up his final shift with Escambia County Fire Rescue on Tuesday, marking the end of a nearly three-decade career in the fire service. Snipes spent 24.5 of those years with Escambia County Fire Rescue, most recently serving as an engine officer at the Cantonment Fire Station. The veteran firefighter's retirement comes after…
item.content:encoded:
Lt. Darren Snipes wrapped up his final shift with Escambia County Fire Rescue on Tuesday, marking the end of a nearly three-decade career in the fire service. Snipes spent 24.5 of those years with Escambia County Fire Rescue, most recently serving as an engine officer at the Cantonment Fire Station.

The veteran firefighter's retirement comes after more than two and a half decades of service to the community. According to the Escambia County Professional Firefighters association, Snipes' tenure reflects the kind of long-term commitment the department relies on to maintain operational readiness and institutional knowledge.

Tuesday marked Snipes' last day working as the Engine 4 officer, a position that puts senior firefighters in leadership roles during emergency response and station operations. The Escambia County Professional Firefighters extended their thanks to Snipes for his years of dedicated service to the county.

item.title: West Roberts Road Reconstruction Pushing Toward Labor Day Reopening
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Crews are making progress on a $4.6 million reconstruction project along West Roberts Road, with the county targeting a post-Labor Day reopening for the stretch between Tate Road and Highway 29. According to Escambia County, new lane closures began August 29 as part of the broader roadway and drainage improvements initiative. Work continued…
item.content:encoded:
Crews are making progress on a $4.6 million reconstruction project along West Roberts Road, with the county targeting a post-Labor Day reopening for the stretch between Tate Road and Highway 29.

According to Escambia County, new lane closures began August 29 as part of the broader roadway and drainage improvements initiative. Work continued through the week, and officials said the road should reopen after the holiday weekend, assuming weather cooperates.

Drivers using West Roberts Road should continue to expect delays and follow posted detour signs in the meantime. The project addresses both pavement rehabilitation and stormwater drainage upgrades for the corridor.

item.title: Escambia, Santa Rosa Turn Damaged Road Signs Into Artificial Reefs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia and Santa Rosa counties are launching a joint initiative to give damaged road signposts a second life—as artificial reefs in the Gulf of Mexico. The "reef-cycling" program will take scrap metal from deteriorated signs and embed them into concrete reef modules that create new underwater habitats for marine life. The partnership brings…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia and Santa Rosa counties are launching a joint initiative to give damaged road signposts a second life—as artificial reefs in the Gulf of Mexico. The "reef-cycling" program will take scrap metal from deteriorated signs and embed them into concrete reef modules that create new underwater habitats for marine life.

The partnership brings together local government agencies, vocational education programs, and environmental organizations focused on coastal stewardship. By repurposing materials that would otherwise end up in landfills, the two counties aim to address waste management while simultaneously enhancing marine ecosystems that support local fishing and tourism.

The initiative reflects a growing trend among Gulf Coast communities seeking practical solutions that serve multiple purposes—reducing waste, supporting educational opportunities through vocational training, and restoring critical fish habitat. Damaged signposts are common along area roads and highways, particularly after severe weather, making them an available and ongoing resource for the project.

item.content:encoded:
The Semmes Girls Softball organization is calling attention to vandalism that struck their park Tuesday night, when a teenage boy reportedly knocked down a gate on the facility's grounds. According to WKRG News 5, a volunteer witnessed the incident and alerted organization leadership to the damage.

The vandalism has prompted the youth sports organization to speak publicly about the incident, raising concerns about security and property protection at the facility. Details about the extent of the damage and whether authorities have identified or charged the suspect remain unclear.

The Semmes area park serves as a home field for the girls' softball program and hosts games and practices throughout the season. The organization has not yet announced any changes to security measures or facility access in response to the incident.

item.title: De-escalation training keeps Alabama officers ready for high-stakes situations
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Law enforcement agencies across the region are investing in specialized training programs designed to help officers defuse tense situations before they turn violent, according to reporting from WKRG News 5. The focus on de-escalation techniques reflects a broader shift in policing strategy, emphasizing communication and crisis management skills…
item.content:encoded:
Law enforcement agencies across the region are investing in specialized training programs designed to help officers defuse tense situations before they turn violent, according to reporting from WKRG News 5.

The focus on de-escalation techniques reflects a broader shift in policing strategy, emphasizing communication and crisis management skills alongside traditional law enforcement tactics. When seconds matter and lives hang in the balance, officers trained in these methods have shown they can talk people down from dangerous situations rather than resort to force.

The Daphne Police Department is among agencies implementing these programs, recognizing that how officers respond in the first moments of a crisis often determines whether the outcome is tragic or whether it gives people a second chance.

For listeners in Pensacola and surrounding communities, similar training initiatives may be underway locally with the Pensacola Police Department and Escambia County Sheriff's Office. De-escalation training has become increasingly standard across Florida law enforcement agencies as departments work to reduce use-of-force incidents and improve community safety outcomes.

item.title: Judge denies dismissal bid in Jehlynn Woods murder case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola man accused of fatally shooting Jehlynn Woods in April will remain charged with murder after a judge rejected his request to dismiss the case, according to WKRG News 5. The defendant claimed he acted in self-defense while protecting his sister, arguing the circumstances warranted dismissal under Florida law. However, the judge found…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola man accused of fatally shooting Jehlynn Woods in April will remain charged with murder after a judge rejected his request to dismiss the case, according to WKRG News 5.

The defendant claimed he acted in self-defense while protecting his sister, arguing the circumstances warranted dismissal under Florida law. However, the judge found the argument insufficient to eliminate the charges at this stage of proceedings.

Woods was killed in April of last year. The case continues through the court system, and prosecutors will move forward with the murder charge against the accused shooter.

item.title: Drive-by shooting at Ninth Ave smoothie shop fuels safety concerns

item.content:encoded: A drive-by shooting outside Vibes and Smoothies on Ninth Avenue Sunday night is raising fresh alarm about the area's security, according to WKRG News 5. The incident marks another violent incident at the location, which has become a frequent destination for police response. Since March, the Pensacola Police Department has responded to calls at that address nearly three dozen times, suggesting an ongoing pattern of disturbances at the popular smoothie shop. Authorities have not yet released details about injuries, suspects, or a motive for the shooting. The repeated incidents at the same location have officers and community members questioning what conditions are driving the string of problems and what measures might address the pattern before another shooting occurs.

item.content:encoded:
Baldwin County residents have a chance to safely dispose of unwanted batteries this Saturday as part of National Battery Take-Back Day. The Solid Waste Disposal Authority is hosting the free event from 7 a.m. to noon, according to WKRG News 5.

The program gives residents an environmentally responsible way to get rid of batteries that might otherwise end up in landfills or regular trash. Battery disposal events help keep hazardous materials out of the waste stream and allow for proper recycling of valuable materials.

While the event is located in Baldwin County, residents in nearby areas may want to check if similar programs are available locally through their own solid waste management authorities.
